en: Seeing you going up this building confirmed it for me.
The old you would never do it this way.
You'd show up at the other building and kill them with your own hands.
But that's not what happened. Because you were scared to face Kiryu-san and the others head on.
You didn't think you'd be strong enough to win out anymore. Am I right?
Chairman Kurosawa. We both stand at the top of organizations 30,000 men strong. You and I should settle this man to man.
I'll pay your way into the afterlife myself. Count on it.
What in the hell... Boss, why's it gotta be you!?
I guess you never had a clue, did you?
I knew it was the right move making you captain.
With a moron like you as my second-in-command, it was easy to fool the rest of the men.
I guess our clever friend over there caught on, though. Right, Katsuya?
Tell me, what's your angle here? I get why you'd want to take down the Tojo Clan.
But Watase and Katsuya depend on you. Why would you do this to them?
Who, these clowns? Hahaha. Unfortunately, I've never been one for sentiment.
I haven't spared them a thought since the moment I became seventh chairman.
What!? And you call yourself a leader!?
They're pawns. Nothing more.
Their only purpose was to die along with you tonight.
Though as sacrificial pawns, they played their part well.
Grr... Rrgh... Grrraaaaaaaaaah!
Boss... Tell me just one thing.
Put us down all ya want, but I gotta know⑬what's the goddamn point of all this?
Watase-aniki...
You're breakin' my heart here...
I followed every order you ever gave me, no matter what.

All I wanted was to do ya proud, to be the finest soldier
in the land... I lived for that!
Why not come to me with this? I don't get it, boss!
Because you're too damned likable.
The hell...?

en:
You don't kiss ass, you don't backstab... All you do is romp
around, following whatever your gut tells you.

Yet people still flock to your side by the dozen...
You win them over all too easily.
The same goes for you, Katsuya. You dress it up differently, but you and Watase are alike.
You think you can run a family based on charisma alone.
Personally... I despise yakuza who are afraid to fight dirty.

Especially punks like you who act above it all and skate by
on charm alone.

Listen. In the end, yakuza are mostly idiots. When you run
a family, it's your job to rule over these simpletons.

Character counts for nothing in this game. Know what happens
to guys like you in this world?
They end up as stains on the organization. And the men who follow them, cannon fodder.
At this rate, every last yakuza's gonna end up being trash in the gutter.
Fighting strong opponents...
Protecting your allies...
Passing on your dreams...
Laying your life on the line...
The dumber the shit you believe in, the dumber the flies you'll attract.
And you can't run an empire with nothing but pests at your disposal.
That's why I won't tolerate your stench any longer.
Guess it's down to us now.
Yeah, looks like it.
Don't take this personally, Saejima.
Heh. Always did want a proper crack at ya. Let's go, Kiryu!
Always wanted a proper crack at ya, Kiryu. You ready for this?

Heh... As long as I don't have to hold back.
Now bring it on!
You got some explainin' to do, Ka-chan!
That shit that went down in Fukuoka, and killin' Majima in Sapporo.
Was that your work? You makin' a play to take over the Tojo Clan?
So that's what you thought after all.
Let me be clear. It wasn't me.
Then why go through the trouble of luring us all up here?
This was the only way to find out who the true mastermind was.
Mastermind?
Right. The one who tried to assassinate Chairman Dojima and Patriarch Madarame in Fukuoka.
The one who killed Goro Majima in Sapporo, and caused the accident in Nagoya that killed Azumi and Takachi, top Tojo and Omi men.
It was all planned by someone who wanted to crush both the Tojo Clan as well as the Omi Alliance.
To hell with this roundabout shit! Spit it out already!
I truly wish I could.
But I have no idea why this person went to such lengths to make us fight each other.
To get to the bottom of this, we have to have a final showdown here.
So we're fighting?
Right. It seems that whoever's pulling our strings intends for us all to die.
But merely killing us isn't enough. It has to be like this, with a battle to the death.
He playin' us against each other?
The Watase Family and Ousaka Enterprises are the two main factions of the Omi Alliance.

Kiryu-san and Saejima-san are pillars of the Tojo Clan.
If the four of us wipe each other out...
It would be easy to walk away with everything, exerting minimal effort.
If you knew what was planned, then why go along with it?
The enemy will never show themselves otherwise.
If my guess is right, they are cautious to the extreme.
I expect they'll show up only once this fight is done.
Then tell me. Who do you think is doing this?
At this point, it won't do us any good to speculate.
All we can do now is fight.
Only the survivors will learn the truth of it all.
This isn't the best place to talk.
I'd rather go somewhere quieter, if that's okay.
You know Public Park 3 on Tenkaichi Street?
I'll be waiting there. Come see me later, all right?
Great. See you there, then.
Hold on, Haruka. You're not actually thinkin' of goin', are ya?

I heard somethin' about a message, but let's be real here,
do you even know that guy?

Then, why? That's shady as hell! We don't have a lot of time
to get ready, either.

But he said it's a message from Uncle Ka⑬ I mean, a message
from someone important.
Oh, do tell! Is it from your boyfriend?
No, it's nothing like that...
Oh, come on! Who's it from!?
Well, it's just... I can't really go into it.
Shadyyy!
Hey now, don't tease the girl.
Everyone?

I need to ask you to give me a little time. I understand
you're worried, Yamaura-san, and I realize the concert is
coming up really soon, but⑬
Well, we don't mind. Right, Mai?

Yeah, I'm fine with it. We're going to be practicing right
up until the concert, anyway.

Might as well get it out of the way now. Just don't forget,
we still have an image to maintain.
Thanks, Azusa-san, Mai-san.

I still don't like it... Just promise you'll be careful,
all right, Haruka?
Remember, your dream's almost within reach.
I promise! Thanks, everyone!
Hey, whaddya think you're doin' here!?

Leave us alone, will ya? You have any idea what you guys
have put us through!?
If you're here to make trouble, then get lost!

Whoa, back off. No need to go losin' your head like that. We
come in peace today.
Oh, yeah? You better have a good reason!

'Course we do. We came to fill ya in on our plan. Our boss's
really stickin' his neck out for this.
Least you could do is hear us out.
...I'm listenin'.

We're cancelin' T-Set's major debut concert at the Japan
Dome tomorrow.
We're holdin' a different event there the day after.
Another event?
Yeah, the debut of a supergroup called Dream Line.

Made up of the winners of the Princess League, T-Set, and
the runner up, Haruka Sawamura.

Made up of the winner of the Princess League, Haruka
Sawamura, and the runners-up, T-Set.
A supergroup?
Dream Line? What's that?

Basically, our president, Katsuya, felt sorry for Dyna
Chair, since Park-san's gone and all.
He wants to promote Haruka along with T-Set.
You're serious?
Heh, we sure are.
We had no problem performing by ourselves, of course.

But the prez and Nakai-san think teaming up with Haruka'd
help create more buzz.
That's great...
Yeah, it'll be great if we can pull it off.
Yeah, I guess it might be great...
What brought this on all of a sudden?

It sounds like Park and our boss had this all planned since
before the Princess League started.
But, uh, I was only told the night before last.
Since before the Princess League!?

I thought Katsuya-han was tossing off ideas at first, but it
sounds to me like it really was planned from the get-go.

Both Park and the boss already signed a contract with a
major record label. The debut song's ready to roll, too.

Why the hell didn't they tell us? We're the ones lookin'
after these kids.
Who drops this on the staff right before a concert?

Look, I hear ya. But it's not like we can take it up with
anybody.

What with all that happened to Park-san, and now our
president as well.
What? Your president, too?

He got into a little accident. He's in surgery at Touto
University Hospital.
Katsuya-san is!?

All I can tell ya is our boss and Park-san were dead serious
about this.

It's our job to trust 'em and make sure this event's a
success.
Don't ya think?
Yamaura?
I have one condition.
Name it.

You guys can handle the event coordination. But we wanna
be involved in the creative end.
Christina and I'll handle the choreography and chorus.
Well, whaddya think? Give us the okay, and we're on board.

Well, it ain't like there's anyone else who could get a song
ready for the stage in as little as a day.
I oughta be the one askin' you.
So that means...?
Yeah. We got a deal.
Yamaura-san?
Oh, sorry to interrupt.
Another problem?
Yeah... Just heard back from the costume supplier.

They said if we're gonna cancel the event, we gotta pay a
penalty to the contributin' brands.

These Tokyo companies'll turn on ya in a second. Always
lookin' to get their cut.

It's tricky, all right. Park-san was handling all the
contracts for the event.

Some companies will no doubt try to overcharge after hearing
she's no longer with us.

We're already scramblin' to get back on our feet after the
event organizer canceled on us.

Not to mention their reason is that Osaka Talent will pay
them more. Can ya believe that!?
We can't let Haruka down, Yamaura.

We want to hold an event in Tokyo soon, yet the stage setup
and location are still undecided.
It must be hard for her to stay motivated.
Oh, no, I'm all right.
There is one thing bothering me, though.
She got this letter before she died, then?

She said she was going to meet her ex-husband after the
concert tomorrow.

For the first time in twenty years, hm? She must have been
quite the romantic.

The way I see it, this Japan Dome concert was probably a
form of closure for Park-san.
Closure?

Yes. She almost stood on stage at the Japan Dome herself
twenty years ago.
But then she had to give up her dream.

I think a part of her was still holding on to that dream,
all these years later.

Maybe she organized the Japan Dome event for me as a way to
finally put that dream to rest.
You mean she still hadn't let go of her idol career?
The same is true for everyone in this line of work.

One day you're the object of everyone's attention, and the
next, nobody even gives you a second glance.

Work offers dissipate, and you leave the industry just
another forgotten soul.

The cruelest part of it is you're the only one who can
decide whether or not to close that chapter of your life.

That's why I want to do Park-san proud up there. I don't
know how far I can take it...
But I want to sing my heart out and give her the closure she deserves.

Yamaura-san, it doesn't matter if it's tomorrow, the next
day, or a year from now.

Will you stick with me until we can hold a concert at the
Japan Dome?

I promise I'll practice more, so I'll be ready when the
time comes.
Heh, I know ya will, Haruka.
Yamaura.
Don't worry, I'm supporting Park-san's dream, too!

I'm not gonna let you rest until you bring the house down at
the Dome!
(Okay, I should get back to the <Color:7>lesson studio<Color:Default>.)
Sorry to take up your time when you're so busy.

It's all right. So, what did Uncle Kaz⑬ I mean, Kiryu-san
say?
Oh, yeah. I'd better pass that on first, huh?

Kiryu-san and I saw an interview with the head of Osaka
Talent on TV last night.

That's when we learned the concert at the Japan Dome had
been canceled.
Kiryu-san said he had a few things to take care of.
He asked me to pass on a message on his behalf.
What did he say?
"Never give up." That's what he wanted me to tell you.
Never give up?

A pretty short message, I know. He probably had a lot more
he wanted to say.

But he didn't have time, so he chose what he thought was
most important.
Hehe... Never give up, huh?
Words to live by, if you ask me.
I'm not sure how you and Kiryu-san know each other.
But I get the feeling he's been rooting for you for a while.
Yes, he has. He's supported me this whole time.

No kidding? Well, it's good to see you're following his
advice already.
